'''Thermal Vent''' is a weapon [[Experimental Effects|Experimental Effect]] for engineered [[Beam Laser|Beam Lasers]]. While the beam is striking a valid target, the weapon reduces the firing ship's heat instead of adding its normal thermal load. The effect can drive the ship below the 20% heat level used for low-temperature anti-xeno tactics, but only while the laser keeps firing and remains on target.<ref name="thermal-vent-edwiki">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Thermal_Vent Thermal Vent], ''Elite Dangerous Wiki''; current mechanics, compatible module family, material recipe, and reported post-Odyssey behaviour. Retrieved 23 September 2026.</ref><ref name="axi-lasers">[https://wiki.antixenoinitiative.com/en/lasers Lasers], Anti-Xeno Initiative; practical Thermal Vent behaviour and limitations in anti-xeno combat. Retrieved 23 September 2026.</ref>

{{Callout
 | type = tip
 | label = Quick answer
 |1=Apply Thermal Vent to an engineered Beam Laser at an Engineer workshop. Keep the beam on a target to cool the ship. The effect does not reduce weapon-capacitor draw and does not add heat or damage to the target.
}}

== Effect ==

Thermal Vent reverses the Beam Laser's heat contribution while the beam is connecting with a target. A hotter-running beam produces more cooling, while a lower-heat beam produces less. Damage falloff also weakens the cooling effect, so range and blueprint choice both matter.<ref name="thermal-vent-edwiki" />

The effect changes the firing ship's heat management. It does not increase the laser's damage, transfer the removed heat to the target, or duplicate the target-heating behaviour of Thermal Shock or the [[Retributor Beam Laser]].

Frontier doubled Thermal Vent's effectiveness in the 3.0 Engineering rework and removed its former 25% increase to the weapon's baseline heat.<ref name="beyond-30">[https://forums.frontier.co.uk/threads/elite-dangerous-beyond-chapter-one-3-0.409060/ Elite Dangerous: Beyond — Chapter One 3.0 patch notes], Frontier Developments; Engineering and Thermal Vent changes. Published 27 February 2018. Retrieved 23 September 2026.</ref>

=== Behaviour while missing ===

The in-game description still warns of increased heat generation when the beam misses. Maintained community testing reports that current Odyssey builds do not generate more heat on a miss than an equivalent Beam Laser without Thermal Vent.<ref name="thermal-vent-edwiki" /> Frontier has not documented that later discrepancy. Commanders should therefore treat an exact miss penalty as unconfirmed rather than planning around the description alone.

== Applying Thermal Vent ==

A Beam Laser must first have an [[Engineering]] blueprint of any grade. Thermal Vent is then applied as a one-time modification at an Engineer workshop; it is not available through Remote Engineering. A weapon can carry only one Experimental Effect at a time.<ref name="experimental-effect">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Experimental_Effect Experimental Effect], ''Elite Dangerous Wiki''; application rules and workshop restriction. Retrieved 10 September 2026.</ref>

The material cost is the same regardless of the weapon's class, mount or blueprint:

Retrieved 23 September 2026.</ref>

Overloaded and Plasma Conversion are Operations-era additions to Live. Their current Engineering records include Thermal Vent among the available effects.<ref name="inara-overloaded">[https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/226/ Beam Laser — Overloaded blueprint], INARA; Live compatibility and Engineer availability. Retrieved 11 September 2026.</ref><ref name="inara-plasma">[https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/203/ Beam Laser — Plasma Conversion blueprint], INARA; Live compatibility and Engineer availability. Retrieved 11 September 2026.</ref>

Compatible Beam Laser variants, including the Retributor Beam Laser, use the same one-effect limit.

== Blueprint interactions ==

The useful cooling rate follows the Beam Laser's thermal load and effective range:

* '''Long Range''' removes damage falloff within the engineered range, allowing useful cooling at distances where an ordinary beam has already lost much of its effect. This is the usual anti-xeno pairing.
* '''Efficient''' lowers the beam's thermal load, so it also lowers the amount of heat Thermal Vent can remove. The reduced distributor draw may still support longer firing time.
* '''Overcharged''' and '''Short Range''' raise thermal load and can produce stronger cooling inside their effective range, but they retain their ordinary power, distributor or range trade-offs.

A gimballed Beam Laser is easier to hold on a moving target and has a higher thermal load than the equivalent fixed mount, giving it a stronger cooling effect. Fixed beams keep their normal lower distributor draw and are still effective when the pilot can maintain contact.<ref name="axi-lasers" />

== Anti-xeno use ==

Thermal Vent Beam Lasers are commonly used to cool a ship while approaching or orbiting a Thargoid Interceptor. Staying below 20% heat makes the ship harder for an Interceptor to track with its main cannon when the usual cold-orbiting conditions are met. Long Range Weapon is useful because it lets the laser begin cooling beyond the Interceptor's three-kilometre engagement distance.<ref name="axi-lasers" />

The beam still draws from the weapon capacitor and occupies a hardpoint. During an attack run, firing anti-xeno weapons may interrupt the cooling beam or create more heat than it can remove. Thermal Vent therefore supplements heat sinks and sound thermal design; it does not replace them in every phase of a fight.<ref name="axi-lasers" />

== Limits ==

* Cooling stops when the beam stops firing or loses contact with a valid target.
* Cooling weakens inside the weapon's damage-falloff region unless Long Range Weapon removes that falloff.
* Thermal Vent does not reduce distributor draw, power draw or the laser's ordinary fitting requirements.
* The effect provides no cooling target when nothing suitable is in the beam's line of fire.
* A Beam Laser fitted with Thermal Vent cannot carry another Experimental Effect at the same time.

== Live and Legacy ==

Thermal Vent and its 3.0 mechanics are available in both Live and Legacy. Overloaded and Plasma Conversion are Live-only Beam Laser blueprints. Reports that the warning about increased miss heat no longer matches observed behaviour refer to current Odyssey builds; equivalent Legacy behaviour has not been established by the cited current testing.
